Question
========

Betrachten Sie die folgenden Modelldefinitionen.
Nur *eine* davon ist korrekt bzw. sinnvoll.
Wählen Sie diese aus!



Hinweise:

- Es ist *ein* Prädiktor im Modell.
- Der Achsenabschnitt ist Null.
- Die Prädiktoren sind z-standardisiert.
- Gehen Sie davon aus, dass Daten und notwendige R-Pakete und sonstige technischen Voraussetzungen erfüllt sind.
- $N()$ meint die Normalverteilung und $E()$ die Exponentialverteilung.


```{r}
beta_mean <- rnorm(n = 1, mean = sample(c(-2, 0, 2)), sd = sample(c(1,2,3))) %>% round(1)
beta1 <- rnorm(n = 2, mean = sample(c(-2, 0, 2)), sd = sample(c(1,2,3))) %>% round(1)
beta_s <- rexp(1) %>% round(1)
if (beta_s < 0.1) beta_s <- 1
s <- rexp(1, rate = sample(c(1, 2, 3))) %>% round(1) 
if (s < 0.1) s <- 1
```


```{r results = "hide"}
def_correct <- c(
  "y_i ",     " \\sim N(\\mu_i, \\sigma)",
  "\\mu_i ",     " = 0 + \\beta_1 x_i",
  "\\beta_1  ", paste0(" \\sim N(", beta_mean,",", beta_s,")"),
  "\\sigma ",  paste0("\\sim E(", s, ")")
)
# the model defintion is a string of length 8, ie., 4 equations with two sides each

assert_that(length(def_correct) == 8, msg = "model definition is not proper")
```



```{r}
print_model_def <- function(mod_def) {
  # mod_def is expected to be a 8 element string where to adjacent elements are LHS and RHS of one equation
  
  eq1 <- paste0(mod_def[1], mod_def[2])  # eq. 1, lhs + rhs
  eq2 <- paste0(mod_def[3], mod_def[4])  # eq. 2, lhs + rhs
  eq3 <- paste0(mod_def[5], mod_def[6])  # eq. 3, lhs + rhs
  eq4 <- paste0(mod_def[7], mod_def[8])  # eq. 4, lhs + rhs
  
  output_string1 <- 
    glue::glue("${eq1}$  ")
   output_string2 <- 
    glue::glue("${eq2}$  ")
    output_string3 <- 
    glue::glue("${eq3}$  ")
       output_string4 <- 
    glue::glue("${eq4}$  ")
  
  cat(output_string1)
  cat("  \n")
  cat(output_string2)
  cat("  \n")
  cat(output_string3)
  cat("  \n")
  cat(output_string4)
  cat("  \n")
}
```






```{r}
permutate_lhs <- function(mod_def) {
  
  lhs_vec <- c(mod_def[1], mod_def[3], mod_def[5], mod_def[7])
  lhs_incorrect<- lhs_vec
  while(str_c(lhs_incorrect, collapse = "\n") == str_c(lhs_vec, collapse = "\n")) {
    lhs_incorrect <- sample(lhs_vec)
  }
  
  mod_def_output <- c(lhs_incorrect[1], mod_def[2],
                      lhs_incorrect[2], mod_def[4],
                      lhs_incorrect[3], mod_def[6],
                      lhs_incorrect[4], mod_def[8])
  
  return(mod_def_output)
}

mod_def2 <- permutate_lhs(def_correct)
```






```{r}
make_sign_neg <- function(mod_def) {
  
  beta_s <- -beta_s
  if (abs(beta_s) < 0.1) beta_s <- -1
  s <- -s
  if (abs(s) < 0.1) s <- -1
  
 out <- c(
  "y_i ",     " \\sim N(\\mu_i, \\sigma)",
  "\\mu_i ",     " = 0 + \\beta_1 x_i",
  "\\beta_1  ", paste0(" \\sim N(", beta_mean,",", beta_s,")"),
  "\\sigma ",  paste0("\\sim E(", s, ")")
)

assert_that(length(out) == 8, msg = "model definition is not proper")
  return(out)
}

mod_def3 <- make_sign_neg(def_correct)
```





```{r}
drop_suffix <- function(mod_def){
  out <- str_remove_all(mod_def, "_i")
  return(out)
}

mod_def4 <- drop_suffix(def_correct)
```




```{r}
replace_tilde <- function(mod_def) {
  
  out <- str_replace_all(mod_def, Hmisc::escapeRegex("\\sim"), "=")
}

mod_def5 <- replace_tilde(def_correct)
```


```{r}
change_intercept <- function(mod_def) {
  out <- str_replace_all(mod_def, pattern = "0", "1")
}

mod_def6 <- change_intercept(def_correct)
```




```{r}
sol_df <-
  tibble(
    id = 1:6,
    correct_answer = c(T, F, F, F, F, F),
    mod_def = list(def_correct, mod_def2, mod_def3, mod_def4, mod_def5, mod_def6),
    explanations = c(
      "korrekt",
      "Die linken Seiten der Gleichungen passen nicht zu den rechten Seiten",
      "Streuungen dürfen kein negatives Vorzeichen haben",
      "Die Indizes i fehlen (bei mu)",
      "Die Tilde-Zeichen sind fälschlich durch Gleichheitszeichen ersetzt",
      "Der Achsenabschnitt ist per Angabe Null"
    )
  ) %>% 
  slice_sample(n = nrow(.)) %>% 
  mutate(id2 = LETTERS[1:nrow(.)])
```
